Rashi on Menachot 13b:11:1.hebrew: התם ממילא - נופל הדם במזרק, הכא שקיל קומץ ורמי בכלי:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:11:1.english: There, by itself - The blood falls into the basin, [whereas] here, he takes the handful and places [it] in a vessel.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:12:1.english: Here too - In the gathering of the frankincense.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:14:1.hebrew: קדושת כלי הוא - דמקדש מקבל דם בכלי, והנותן בכלי מקדש, ה"נ קומץ בכלי, ובדבר זה דומין. אבל ליקוט לבונה, דלא דמי לחדא מהנך, לאו עבודה היא:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:14:1.english: It is the sanctification of a vessel - For one who receives blood in a vessel sanctifies [it], and one who places [the handful] into a vessel sanctifies [it]; so too, one who scoops with a vessel [sanctifies], and in this matter they are similar. But the collection of the frankincense, which does not resemble any of these, is not a sacrificial rite.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:15:1.hebrew: שני כבשים - כבשי עצרת, דכתיב: ושני כבשים בני שנה לזבח שלמים (ויקרא כ״ג:י״ט), ואותם כבשים מתירין ומקדשין לשתי הלחם. ואע"ג דז' כבשים ופר ואילים שנים ושעיר עזים כתיבי התם, מפרש בפרק התכלת (לקמן מנחות מז.) שאין הלחם קדוש אלא בשחיטת שני כבשים שלמים, הואיל והוזקקו עמו בתנופה:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:15:1.english: Two lambs - The lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot], as it is written: "And two yearling lambs for a sacrifice of peace offerings" (Leviticus 23:19), and those lambs permit and sanctify the two loaves. And even though seven lambs, a bull, two rams, and a goat kid are written there, it is explained in the chapter "HaTechelet" (below, Menachot 47a) that the loaves are sanctified only through the slaughter of the two peace-offering lambs, since they were bound with it in the waving.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:15:2.english: That loaf or that arrangement, etc. - And the reason of Rabbi Yosei is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:16:1.english: The left thigh has not become piggul - And one who eats it is not liable to karet.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:17:1.english: If one limb became impure - After it was separated from the [rest of the] meat.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:18:1.english: There is never [liability for] karet in it - In the other loaf, concerning which he did not have [improper] intent.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:18:2.hebrew: עד שיפגל בשתיהן החלות בכזית - כלומר, אפילו לא פיגל אלא בכזית בין שתיהן, הוי כולהו פיגול:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:18:2.english: Unless he has intent of piggul with regard to both of them, the loaves, with an olive-bulk - That is to say, even if he only had intent of piggul with regard to an olive-bulk between the two of them, they are all piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:18:3.english: With regard to one of them - Its fellow [loaf] is not rendered piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:19:1.english: Even with one of them as well - For it states in the mishna: "[Both] this and that are piggul."

Rashi on Menachot 13b:19:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא - גבי יריכות, דמזבח אחד אתו, חד גופא נינהו, ואי פיגל בזו נתפגלה זו; משום הכי מצטרפות חלות: חצי זית מזו וחצי זית מזו כי ערבינהו, דחישב על מנת לאכול כזית למחר בין שתיהן, דמהני להו מה שעירבו זה במחשבתו כאילו באו שתיהן מגוף אחד, דאמרינן לקמן (מנחות דף יד:) דעירב מחשבתו מהני לצרפן. וגבי חלות, ה"ט דבאחת מהן לא נתפגלה חבירתה: משום דלא מחד גופא אתו, ובמחשבתו נמי לא עירבן:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:19:2.english: Granted, if you say - With regard to the thighs, which come from one sacrifice, they are one body, and if one had intent of piggul with regard to this one, that one became piggul; due to that, the loaves combine — half an olive-bulk from this one and half an olive-bulk from that one — when he combined them, [namely,] where he intended to eat an olive-bulk tomorrow between both of them, for that which he combined them in his thought is effective for them, [treating them] as though both of them came from one body, as we say later (Menachot 14b) that [when] he combined [them in] his thought, it is effective to combine them. And with regard to the loaves, this is the reason that with [intent regarding] one of them its fellow [loaf] was not rendered piggul: because they did not come from one body, and in his thought he also did not combine them.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:1:1.hebrew: קמ"ל דבהא מודה - דטעמא לאו משום הכי הוא, אלא משום דמפרש לקמן: אין מתיר מפגל מתיר:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:1:1.english: It teaches us that in this [case] he concedes - That the reason is not because of that, but rather because of what [the Gemara] explains below: A permitting factor does not render [another] permitting factor piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:2:1.english: Rabbi Yosei would say - That is to say, this is the reason of Rabbi Yosei:

Rashi on Menachot 13b:2:2.hebrew: אין מתיר מפגל את המתיר - אין עבודת מתיר זה, כגון קומץ, מועלת לפגל מתיר האחר, הלבונה, במחשבה שהוא מחשב על הלבונה בעבודת הקומץ:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:2:2.english: A permitting factor does not render [another] permitting factor piggul - The service of this permitting factor, such as the handful, is not effective to render the other permitting factor, the frankincense, piggul through an intention that he contemplates concerning the frankincense during the service of the handful.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:3:1.hebrew: וכן אתה אומר בבזיכי לבונה - שאם הקטיר האחד מבזיכי לחם הפנים ע"מ להקטיר האחר למחר, אינה מחשבה לפגל:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:3:1.english: And so you say with regard to the bowls of frankincense - That if one burned one of the bowls of the shewbread with the intention to burn the other tomorrow, it is not an intention that renders [it] piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:4:1.hebrew: מאי וכן - פשיטא, דכל היכא דאיכא שני מתירין פליג ר' יוסי:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:4:1.english: What is "And so" - It is obvious, for wherever there are two permitting factors, Rabbi Yosei disagrees.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:4:2.english: It is not of the same kind as the meal offering - For this is fine flour and that is frankincense.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:6:1.hebrew: אינה בעיכוב מנחה - כלומר, לעולם טעמא משום דאין מתיר מפגל את המתיר. וה"ק להו: הזבח כולו אחד, והדם הוא מתיר את האימורים; הלכך כי חישב על האימורים חוץ לזמנו בשעת עבודת דם, לאו שני מתירין נינהו. אבל לבונה אינה מעכבת מנחה — אינה בכלל עכוב שירים, ואין הקומץ מעכב הלבונה מהקטיר כי היכי דמעכב שיריים; הילכך הויא לבונה מתיר בפני עצמו, ואמר: אין מתיר מפגל את המתיר:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:6:1.english: It is not in the preclusion of the meal offering - That is to say, actually the reason [for Rabbi Yosei's opinion] is because a permitting factor does not render [another] permitting factor piggul. And this is what he was saying to them: An animal offering is entirely one [entity], and the blood is what permits the sacrificial portions [to be burned on the altar]; therefore, when he had an intention regarding the sacrificial portions [to burn them] beyond their designated time during the service of the blood, they are not two permitting factors. However, the frankincense does not preclude the meal offering — [that is,] it is not included in the preclusion of the remainder, and the handful does not preclude the frankincense from being burned [on the altar] in the way that it precludes the remainder [from being eaten]; consequently, the frankincense is an independent permitting factor, and [therefore Rabbi Yosei] says: A permitting factor does not render [another] permitting factor piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:7:1.hebrew: היכא דלא איקבעו בחד מנא - כגון גבי כבשי עצרת, דמודו רבנן בסיפא דמתני': שחט אחד מן הכבשים לאכול מחבירו למחר, שניהם כשרים, דשניהם מתירין את הלחם. התם ודאי אמר: אין מתיר מפגל את המתיר:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:7:1.english: Where they were not fixed in one vessel - For example, in the case of the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot], where the Rabbis concede in the latter clause of the mishna: [If] one slaughtered one of the lambs [with intent] to partake of the other tomorrow, both are fit, as both of them permit the bread [the two loaves]. There, [the Gemara] certainly says: A permitting factor does not render [another] permitting factor piggul.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:8:1.english: The collection of the frankincense - For after the burning of the handful, [the priest] would collect the frankincense from upon the fine flour and burn it.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:8:2.hebrew: משום הולכה נגעו בה - שזה שליקטה ונתנה לכהן, מיעט בהילוך הכהן. והולכה אחת מן העבודו', דגמרי' מזבחים, דכתיב בהו הולכה, דכתיב: והקריבו בני אהרן. ואע"ג דאמר מר (זבחים דף ד.): זו קבלת הדם, אפ"ה לשון הולכה הוא, כדאמרינן בסוף הכל חייבין בראייה (חגיגה יא.):
Rashi on Menachot 13b:8:2.english: Because of conveying they touched upon it - For this [non-priest], who collected it and gave it to the priest, reduced the walking of the priest. And conveying is one of the [sacrificial] services, as we derive from animal offerings, regarding which conveying is written, as it is written: "And Aaron's sons shall present [the blood]." And even though the Master said (Zevachim 4a): "This is the receiving of the blood," nevertheless it is a term of conveying, as we say at the end of [the chapter] Hakol Chayavin BiRe'iyah (Chagigah 11a).

Rashi on Menachot 13b:8:3.hebrew: שלא ברגל - כגון זר שלא זז ממקומו, אלא ליקט והושיטה לכהן:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:8:3.english: Not by foot - For example, a non-priest who did not move from his place, but rather collected [the frankincense] and extended it to a priest.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:9:1.english: We have learned - That the collection of the frankincense is a [sacrificial] service.

Rashi on Menachot 13b:9:2.hebrew: זה הכלל - בפ"ק, וקחשיב להנך ד' עבודות חשובות. קומץ דמי לשוחט, דזה נוטל ומפריש חלק לגבוה מחלק כהנים, וכן זה:
Rashi on Menachot 13b:9:2.english: This is the principle - [This mishna is taught] in the first chapter [12a], and it enumerates those four significant rites. Removing the handful is comparable to slaughtering, for this one takes and separates a portion for the Most High from the priests' portion, and so too does the other.

Tosafot on Menachot 13b:15:1.hebrew: לאכול אחד מן הסדרים - הוא הדין חלה אחת מן הסדרים, שאותו הסדר פיגול, מדבעי רבי יוחנן בגמ': בלחמי תודה מהו? במנחת מאפה תנור מהו? משמע דמיבעיא ליה משום דהוו שני מינים, אבל אותו מין פשיטא דנתפגל. והא דקאמרינן בגמרא: אילו איטמא חד אבר מי איטמא כוליה? אע"ג דשייך האי טעמא בחלה אחת, שאם נטמאה אחת לא נטמא כל הסדר, מ"מ לענין פיגול נתפגל, הואיל והוקבעו בסדר אחד, וחשיב כחד לענין פיגול, טפי מפיגל בירך של ימין דלא נתפגל ירך שמאל. ושמא גם לענין טומאה, אם נטמאה אחת נטמא כל הסדר. והא דנקט הכא ובסיפא אחד מן הסדרים, ולא נקט חלה אחת מאחד מן הסדרים, משום רבותא דר"י, ובסיפא משום רבותא דחכמים; דאע"פ שחישב על כל הסדר, אפ"ה אותו סדר דוקא פיגול וטמא, והשני אינו פיגול וטהור:
Tosafot on Menachot 13b:15:1.english: To partake of one of the arrangements - The same law applies [if one intended to partake of] one loaf of the arrangements, that that [entire] arrangement is piggul, since Rabbi Yoḥanan raises a dilemma in the Gemara: Regarding the loaves of a thanks offering, what is [the halakha]? Regarding a baked meal offering of an oven, what is [the halakha]? This implies that he raises the dilemma [only] because they are two [different] types; but [with regard to loaves of] that same type, it is obvious that it is rendered piggul. And as for that which we say in the Gemara: "If one limb became impure, did the whole [animal] become impure?" — even though this reasoning applies [as well] to a single loaf, that if one became impure the entire arrangement did not become impure, nevertheless regarding piggul it is rendered piggul, since they were established in one arrangement, and it is considered like one [entity] regarding piggul, more than [the case of] one who had piggul intent regarding the right thigh, where the left thigh was not rendered piggul. And perhaps even regarding ritual impurity, if one [loaf] became impure, the entire arrangement becomes impure. And as for that which [the Tanna] taught here and in the latter clause "one of the arrangements", and did not teach "one loaf from one of the arrangements" — [here it is] to demonstrate the novel ruling of Rabbi Yosei, and in the latter clause to demonstrate the novel ruling of the Rabbis: that even though he had intent regarding the entire arrangement [or an entire arrangement was affected], even so, specifically that arrangement is piggul and impure, while the second [arrangement] is not piggul and is pure.

Tosafot on Menachot 13b:19:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא חד גופא - נראה דהשתא נמי ס"ל, דהא דמצטרפין כי ערבינהו היינו מטעם דדרשינן לקמן (מנחות דף יד:): הכתוב עשאן גוף אחד והכתוב עשאן שני גופין. ומש"ה פריך: אי אמרת בשלמא דשתי ירכות חשיבי חד גופא, דאם פיגל בזו נתפגלה זו, מש"ה מצטרף כמו כשמערב, דהכתוב עשאן גוף אחד; אלא אי אמרת דשתי ירכות נמי חשיבי תרי גופי, מה מועיל מה שעשאן הכתוב גוף אחד? דאפשר נמי דלמאי דקסבר רב הונא, אם חישב בשתי הירכות בכזית לא הוי פיגול, אם איתא דחשיבא לאחר שהובדלו זו מזו. וצ"ע. ובקונטרס פירש בע"א:
Tosafot on Menachot 13b:19:1.english: Granted if you say [that they are] one body - It appears that now too, [the Gemara] maintains that this [rule] that they [the half-olive-bulk piggul intentions concerning the two bowls of frankincense] combine when one physically mixed them [the frankincense of the two bowls together] is on account of that which we expound below (Menachot 14b): The verse made them one body, and the verse made them two bodies. And for this reason [the Gemara] asks: Granted if you say that the two thighs are considered one body, such that if he had piggul intention regarding this one, that one became piggul, for this reason [the intention concerning the two bowls of frankincense] combines [to form an olive-bulk], just as when one physically mixes [the frankincense of the two bowls together], since the verse made them one body; but if you say that the two thighs are also considered two bodies, what does it help that the verse made them one body? For it is also possible that according to what Rav Huna maintains, if he had intention in both thighs [amounting to] an olive-bulk, it would not be piggul, if it is so that they are considered [two bodies] once they have been separated from one another. And [this matter] requires further study. And in the Kuntres [Rashi], it was explained in a different manner.

Tosafot on Menachot 13b:1:1.hebrew: קמ"ל דבהאי מודה - והא דבעי למימר בסמוך דר' יוסי דלא כר"מ דאמר מפגלין בחצי מתיר, לא דמי; דהכא קומץ המנחה חשיב עבודה שלמה, כיון שאין כיוצא בה בלבונה, כדמוכח בכוליה פירקין לקמן. וכך פירש בקונטרס בסמוך:
Tosafot on Menachot 13b:1:1.english: It teaches us that in this [case] he concedes - And as for that which [the Gemara] wants to say shortly, that Rabbi Yosei is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says [that] one renders [an offering] piggul with half of a permitting factor — it is not comparable; for here, [taking] the handful of the meal offering is considered a complete service, since there is no [service] corresponding to it with the frankincense, as is proven throughout our entire chapter below. And so explained Rashi nearby.

Tosafot on Menachot 13b:8:1.hebrew: משום הולכה נגעו בה קסבר הולכה שלא ברגל כו' - בסוף פ"ק דזבחים (דף יג:), שמעתי שטבילת אצבע מפגלת, וחד טעמא הוא, דמסיק עלה אף אנן נמי תנינא כי הכא; ואפ"ה לא קאמר עלה: קסבר הולכה שלא ברגל הוא:
Tosafot on Menachot 13b:8:1.english: It is because of conveying that they touched upon it; he holds [that] conveying without [movement of] the foot, etc. - At the end of the first chapter of Zevachim (13b), [regarding the statement,] "I heard that dipping of the finger renders [an offering] piggul," and it is one [and the same] rationale, for [the Gemara] concludes regarding it, "We have also learned [this in a mishna]," just as here; and nevertheless, [the Gemara] did not say regarding it: "He holds [that] conveying without [movement of] the foot is [conveying]."
